title: Time, Date, Duration
preamble:
# Time, Date, Duration

The temporal types (`Time`, `Date`,
`Duration`), the builtins that operate on them, and the
integrator-owned timezone-resolution contract.

Duration values are `time`-dimensioned unit literals — `1_h`,
`30_min`, `500_ms` — with no separate duration-literal token. This
doc formalises the `Duration` type and the rest of the temporal
surface.

Paired with:
- [LSTR] for `t.to_string(format)`.
- [LDET] for the engine-controlled
  `now()` clock.
- [LLEX] for duration-literal lexing.
- [LADP] for adapter wire-
  format obligations.

## What this is not

- Not a calendar library. Operations beyond the listed surface
  (business-day arithmetic, holiday awareness, timezone
  database, period-of-day calculations) are out of scope.
- Not a tzdata bundle. libds carries no timezone database; the
  integrator owns resolution per [LTIM.10].
- Not a parser. DS writes temporal values as text and reads none:
  a host or an adapter delivers them typed ([LTIM.11.2]), and the
  `calendar` module builds them from integer fields ([LTIM.14]).
